item.title: His Phone And Wallet Were In The Wreck. He Wasn’t.
item.description: College student Bryce Laspisa, 19, told his mother he was stopping to sleep during his drive home. Hours later, on August 30, 2013, his SUV was found overturned near California’s Castaic Lake, with his belongings inside. Extensive searches failed to locate him, and he remains missing.

item.title: His Boat Was Empty. He Was Found Tied To Its Anchor.
item.description: Florida school librarian Patrick Mullins, 52, disappeared during a boating trip in January 2013. Nine days later, he was found shot dead and tied to an anchor. Investigators found no blood in his boat, and the medical examiner could not determine whether his death was homicide or suicide.

item.title: His Son Died In A Hot Car. His Conviction Was Overturned
item.description: Cooper Harris, 22 months old, died in his father’s SUV in Georgia in June 2014. Justin Ross Harris’s murder conviction was overturned in 2022 because improperly admitted evidence prejudiced his trial. Prosecutors dismissed the charges relating to Cooper’s death in 2023.

item.title: Police Sent Her Into A Sting. Then They Lost Her
item.description: Rachel Hoffman, 23, was killed during a Tallahassee police sting in May 2008 after officers lost contact with her. Both killers received life sentences. Her death prompted Florida’s Rachel’s Law, establishing safeguards for confidential informants.

item.title: He Said She Left. She Was Buried In His Backyard.
item.description: Zoe Campos, 18, vanished from Lubbock, Texas, in 2013. Carlos Rodriquez told police she had left his home, but five years later, he confessed and led detectives to her remains in his former backyard. He pleaded guilty to murder and was sentenced to life in 2022.

item.title: The Toxicology Report Her Husband Refused To Believe
item.description: Diane Schuler’s wrong-way crash on New York’s Taconic State Parkway killed eight people, including herself, in July 2009. Tests found a blood-alcohol level of 0.19% and marijuana in her system. Her husband disputed the findings, but independent retesting confirmed them.

item.title: Haleigh Was Missing. A Cinder Block Held The Door Open
item.description: Five-year-old Haleigh Cummings disappeared from her Satsuma, Florida, home in February 2009, with the back door reportedly propped open by a cinder block. Investigators later classified the case as a homicide, but Haleigh remains missing and no one has been charged in her disappearance.

item.title: Police Suspected The Missing Father Until They Found Him
item.description: When Elaine Dardeen and her two children were found murdered near Ina, Illinois, in November 1987, investigators initially suspected her missing husband, Keith. His body was discovered a mile away the next day. Despite a later confession from serial killer Tommy Lynn Sells, the murders remain unsolved.
